That is exactly when the server refuses it, because the spec grants only on `=== true` (permission.zod.ts:196, :218). The anonymous default and the no-provider fail-open are unchanged.
Metadata-protocol: none
Responsibility: `the console's permission check, which reads an absent CRUD bit as allowed` | `@objectstack/spec's objectPermissionGrants (=== true) and the served /me/permissions rows` | `every user with a read-only or partial set (auditor, read-only finance) who is offered actions the server then refuses with 403`
Thread-read: 6420760374
Premise: corrected 2026-10-26T16:26Z — on `origin/main` `df8aac41f2` both suspected causes are ruled out by the code. (1) Loading: the provider renders only its fallback until data arrives (MePermissionsProvider.tsx:456), and `check` fails closed without data (:368). (2) View All does not cascade, because `check` maps `create → allowCreate` (:373). What remains is the polarity: `:386 objPerm[k] !== false`. The server's plain-wildcard coverage (core `effective-object-permissions.ts:364–371`) copies only `true` bits, so a read-only `'*': { allowRead: true }` set serves `{ allowRead: true }` with no `allowCreate`. The client allows it and the server refuses it. This is code diverging from spec, so the client aligns to the spec (protocol is the baseline), with no decision box.
Serial constraints cleared: none — no open PR touches `ui/packages/permissions` or `permissions.json`.
Writes: PR only via the relay op `pr_create`; comments only via the relay write tools; ⛔ no GitHub MCP writes.

- **Ruling section:** 6416233738 Q3 item 7 (New hidden or greyed without Create; reproduce with the auditor set and pin the verdict).
- **Seat's route:**
  - With data loaded and authenticated, an object row's CRUD bit is allowed only when it is `=== true`, in `check` and in `checkField`'s object-level fallback. Lowercase the object key in `check` as `checkField` already does.
  - Keep `data.authenticated !== true` for anonymous and the no-provider `can: () => true`.
  - Reproduce first: an auditor / read-only `'*'` fixture gives `listNew` allowed before the fix and denied after. Also pin Edit / Delete on the same fixture.
  - Re-run `affordanceGrantMap-12082` (plugin-form) and the permissions suite. Any fixture that relied on absent-means-allowed gets explicit bits, and each flip is listed in the report.
  - `Fixes #26193`.
